messages:
maria: FYI customer 'acme' reported SSO failures right after their IdP cert rotation ~03:14 UTC. Users get a 403 at login. Error in our logs says 'Recipient mismatch' and 'AssertionConsumerService URL not allowed'.

jordan: Can you paste the tenant id + raw SAMLResponse error snippet? Also did they rotate to an ECDSA cert only? @kai might know parser quirks.

maria: Tenant: acme-123. Raw error snippet from our auth proxy: 
```
SAML validation failed: Recipient does not match ACS. expected https://login.redwood.example/sso/acs but got https://app.acme.example/sso/acs
AssertionConsumerService URL not allowed for this ServiceProvider
```
I also pulled the IdP metadata URL they provided: https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml — it shows two KeyDescriptor entries (RSA first, then ECDSA).

infra-bot: created support-ticket #SUP-2026 for tenant acme-123 (priority P1)

kai: Two quick checks: 1) The common failure here is our metadata fetch + proxy host-rewrite. If the ACS host is getting rewritten by a CDN/LB to app.acme.example we reject the Recipient. 2) Ordering of KeyDescriptor sometimes makes our parser pick the wrong signing key when IdP rotates (we expect the active key first).

jordan: Can you run a diagnostic fetch and show the <EntityDescriptor> + KeyDescriptor order? Example: 
```
curl -sS https://idp.acme.example/metadata.xml | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,120p'
```
Also check the X-Forwarded-Host header path through their LB.

maria: output attached (paste): 
```
<EntityDescriptor entityID="https://idp.acme.example">
  <IDPSSODescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <!-- RSA key (old) -->
    </KeyDescriptor>
    <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
      <!-- ECDSA key (new) -->
    </KeyDescriptor>
  </IDPSSODescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>
```
We tried clicking Fetch Metadata from Console — it pulled the same file. Still failing.

kai: Okay, two remediation paths: A) Short-term workaround: upload the metadata XML manually to the tenant in the Console (it bypasses fetch ordering) and then clear the metadata cache. B) Longer fix: make parser pick the key with newer ValidFrom/KeyName or accept dual-key order. For now do A.

jordan: How to clear cache: from our support toolkit run: 
```
supportctl refresh-metadata --tenant acme-123 --force
# or if you need direct patch (k8s):
kubectl -n sso patch configmap redwood-sso-config -p '{"data":{"metadata_reload":"$(date +%s)"}}'
```
Note: run in prod-readonly shell, then watch logs in auth-proxy.

maria: I uploaded the metadata XML manually via Console and ran supportctl refresh-metadata. Watching logs now... still a few 403s but decreasing.

jordan: If it persists after manual upload, confirm ACS host normalization rule. We have a host-rewrite rule in edge that rewrites to app.{tenant}.example; if ACS is strict recipient we need to accept both canonical host and rewritten host or normalize RelayState.

kai: I'll open an eng issue for parser ordering: ENG-SSO-547. Tagging eng-auth for follow-up. For now add a bullet to the support playbook to prefer manual upload when metadata contains dual KeyDescriptor.

maria: Customer confirms logins working for 95% of users now. Remaining sessions were old cookies. I'll close the ticket once they validate. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: support-ticket #SUP-2026 updated: status -> monitoring

maria: Closing note for the thread — root cause: IdP rotated to ECDSA but kept RSA in metadata (old key first). Our fetch+parser picked the old key ordering which confused signature selection and combined with edge host-rewrite produced Recipient mismatch. Remediation: manual metadata upload + forced metadata reload cleared it. Filed ENG-SSO-547 to make parser resilient.

jordan: Nice work. Marking postmortem not required but add a quick note in support runbook.

maria: will do, adding steps to runbook and linking SUP-2026 to ENG-SSO-547. :tada:
